message:
[Page 2] Hiring and onboarding Hiring managers open roles and run their own candidates: Priya for engineering and design roles, Dev for sales. A candidate moves from applied to a phone screen, interviews, an offer, and then hired, or is rejected at any point. Anyone at Fernwood can see the open roles and refer someone. Interviewers write a scorecard after every interview. Offers above the salary band for the role need Wade's approval before they go out. When someone is hired, Aisha Khan plans their first week: a plan with tasks for IT (Jon Bell sets up the laptop and accounts), the manager and a buddy. A new starter gets their software seats (Slack, Google Workspace, 1Password and the tools their team uses) in our tools list, which Jon keeps. [Page 5] Hiring policy Every opening has a hiring manager, a team and a salary band. The hiring manager moves candidates through the stages: applied, phone screen, interview, offer, hired; or rejected at any stage. Each interview has one interviewer, who is asked for a scorecard (1 to 4) the day of the interview. [Page 6] Hiring policy (continued) An offer above the top of the role's salary band needs Wade Wilson's approval before it is sent. When a candidate is hired, the opening is marked filled. Everyone at Fernwood may see the open roles and refer a candidate. Tables attached (name, header and row count; the cells are data too): "Candidate","Email","Position","Stage","Applied On","Source","Offer Amount","Start Date"
Latest message from Wade Wilson: Set up Hiring: Openings, candidates and interviews. Each opening has a hiring manager, a team and a salary band. Candidates move from applied to phone screen, interview, offer and hired, or are rejected at any stage. Priya runs engineering and design roles and Dev runs sales roles. Each interview has one interviewer who writes a scorecard from 1 to 4. Everyone at Fernwood can see open roles and refer a candidate. Its rules, from the policies: - An offer above the top of the role's salary band waits for Wade's approval before it is sent. - On the day of each interview, the interviewer is asked for a scorecard from 1 to 4. - When a candidate is hired, the opening is marked filled. - When a candidate is hired, a first-week plan starts in Onboarding with their name, start date and manager. Its rows come from candidates.csv, imported into its first sheet. The file's columns fill plain columns of that sheet (text, dates, amounts, people, choices, steps); a link can't be filled from a file, so a link column there stays empty for imported rows.
